master noun

an owner; the one in charge of a house, an animal, a slave

also owner, master of the house, proprietor, landlord, mistress

classical

Cic. Off. 1.139: nec domō dominus, sed dominō domus honestanda est
Cato Agr. 5.3 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 162, 282: boss (owner), dominus

dominus, dominī m.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

master, owner

The owner of a house, an estate, a slave or an animal, and so a lord and ruler; a woman is domina. In Christian Latin Dominus is the Lord; in address it is polite, “sir” (Lewis & Short). For the boss who employs one, see employer.

Other words

  • erus, erī m. — master (of slaves and servants)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 141, Trin. 2.4.34; Cic. Off. 2.24 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    The master of the household as his slaves speak of him; the mistress is era. Chiefly in comedy, where the slaves’ erus major and erus minor are the old and the young master (Plaut. As. 2.2.63, Lewis & Short). Lewis & Short prefers the spelling without h.

  • possessor, possessōris m. — an owner, a possessor (of property)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 5.20; Quinct. 30: bonōrum (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    The one who holds property, especially land; in post-Augustan law also the defendant who holds what is claimed (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nec domō dominus, sed dominō domus honestanda est

    the master should not be honoured by his house, but the house by its masterCic. Off. 1.139 (Lewis & Short)

  • Quis est dominus hujus canis?

    Who owns this dog?composed

See also own, employer, master, master, tenant.
